objective: Simplify the unshipped Phase 3 audit actor data migration across Assistant, Endpoint, Integration, and Web by replacing batched procedures and metrics with direct SQL backfills and removing SQL-text Go tests.
acceptance_criteria: Assistant, Endpoint, and Web preflight every audited table, then copy legacy created_by and updated_by values into user actor fields without unknown fallback classification.
Integration historical rows use unknown creation actors because the schema has no legacy actor ID.
No Phase 3 migration creates or references audit_actor_migration_metrics or a backfill procedure.
All Go tests under service migration directories and the callcontext migration SQL-text test are removed at the user's direction.

Executable PostgreSQL migration validation replaces every removed contract, including exhaustive table inventory, successful mapping, invalid-ID failure before updates, final constraints and triggers, call-context schema and rollback, organization credential fingerprint storage, removed legacy columns, and removed registry tables.
The existing four-database rollback validator passes.
out_of_scope: Runtime authentication or actor propagation changes
Application schema shape, actor constraints, immutability triggers, or legacy-column cleanup semantics; removal of migration-internal procedure and metrics objects is in scope
Protobuf, SDK, UI, or Document API changes
Unrelated Redis, docs, or example worktree changes

ownership.service migration SQL: Direct backfill statements and removal of procedure/metrics infrastructure
ownership.migration Go tests: Removal of SQL-text assertions from migration packages
ownership.callcontext migration test: Removal of migration-file inspection from the runtime package
ownership.RFC evidence: Plan, confirmation, verification, and review records

required_tests: Full-history PostgreSQL migration verification for all four services
Exhaustive audited-table inventory plus user-ID mapping and null-update assertions
Call-context snapshot schema and rollback assertions
Organization credential fingerprint-only and registry-removal assertions
Additive expansion, lock timeout, irreversible-down guidance, registry constraints and ordering, and credential uniqueness assertions
Relevant Go package tests and formatting

verification_assertions.assistant-api: Every audited table is listed exactly once; positive legacy created_by and updated_by values become matching user actors; null updated_by remains a null actor pair.
verification_assertions.endpoint-api: Every audited table is listed exactly once; positive legacy created_by and updated_by values become matching user actors; null updated_by remains a null actor pair.
verification_assertions.web-api: Every audited table is listed exactly once; positive legacy created_by and updated_by values become matching user actors; null updated_by remains a null actor pair; credential storage remains fingerprint-only; registry tables remain absent.
verification_assertions.integration-api: Historical rows become unknown creation actors with null IDs because no legacy user ID exists.
verification_assertions.invalid-data: A null or non-positive legacy creation user ID, or a non-positive non-null update ID, fails preflight before any backfill update runs.
verification_assertions.callcontext: Authentication snapshot columns are added, auth_token is preserved, and rollback removes only the snapshot columns.
verification_assertions.removed-tests: Executable PostgreSQL checks preserve additive expansion, lock timeout/reset, irreversible-down guidance, organization credential constraints and uniqueness, registry constraints and dependency-safe removal ordering.

principles.kiss: Use one preflight and direct UPDATE statements instead of persisted procedures, batching, metrics, and resumability machinery.
principles.yagni: Do not retain interruption-resume infrastructure for an unshipped one-time migration.
principles.single_ownership: Each service migration owns its explicit table updates; the shell validator owns executable contract checks; the release owner owns the deployment readiness receipt.
principles.explicit_contracts: Legacy audit IDs are user IDs; Integration has no legacy actor identity; invalid source data fails migration.
principles.fail_safe: Actor-pair constraints reject invalid copied IDs and the verifier includes a failure case.
principles.observability: Migration success is determined by migration exit status plus executable schema and data assertions rather than a persistent metrics table.
principles.least_privilege: No security permissions or runtime trust boundaries change.
principles.reversibility: The existing same-point four-database backup and previous-release rollback procedure remains authoritative; deployment is blocked until its owner and backup identity are recorded.

risks: Direct updates may hold locks longer than the removed batched procedure; deployment requires fenced writes, recorded table sizes, and a production-sized rehearsal with an approved duration.
Rewriting migration files is unsafe if any affected version has already been applied outside this unshipped feature branch.
Invalid legacy IDs now fail closed instead of being converted to unknown.
Integration history remains unknown because no source user ID exists.
approval_conditions: Exact-digest user approval attests that populated legacy audit IDs are user IDs, all legacy creation IDs are positive and non-null, all non-null update IDs are positive, and no affected Phase 3 migration version has been deployed.

Implementation and commit may proceed after exact-digest approval; deployment remains blocked until the release owner approves rfcs/0003-simplify-audit-backfill.operational-readiness.json with row counts, rehearsal duration, maximum duration, backup identity, and rollback owner.
